$comment: Framework migration manifest. The upgrade skill loads this, subtracts the project's migrations.json ledger, and replays outstanding steps by applyMode. Steps are idempotent / skipIfPresent so cold-start replay no-ops already-satisfied changes. See docs/storage-contract.md § Migrations.

releases.summary: Story and ticket split into two artifacts — a PM-owned requirement in the doc store, an engineer-owned implementation in the task store. requirements.storyHome is removed: the story is always the requirement doc in the doc store, whose provider may be tracker-backed. The estimate applies per-ticket (oversight level), no longer as a story-split gate.

steps.description: Remove requirements.storyHome from storage.json. The two-artifact model (story = requirement doc, ticket = work item) makes the docs-vs-tasks toggle incoherent — the story is now always the requirement doc in the doc store. Also migrate conventions.requirementIdFormat from the legacy {storyHome.id} token to {story.id} (same meaning: use whatever the doc store calls the story). Pure config cleanup for the default (storyHome=docs) case; drop the now-empty requirements block.
steps.skipIfPresent: requirements.storyHome absent and requirementIdFormat does not use the {storyHome.id} token

steps.description: Only for a project whose removed storyHome was "tasks" (stories lived as tracker issues): the requirement now belongs in the doc store. Two paths, the user's choice — (a) back the doc store with that tracker, so stories stay as requirement-type issues and delivery tickets remain separate work items, or (b) move the story bodies into the configured doc store as Story docs, keeping their existing IDs as citations. Guided because it rewrites where requirements resolve. No-op when the prior storyHome was docs.
steps.skipIfPresent: prior storyHome was docs, or no requirement issues remain in the task store

releases.summary: Glossary becomes the core term spine (single canonical home for every domain term); ADR is the one optional doc type via docs.types.

steps.description: Introduces docs.types — an optional array enabling the ADR doc type beyond the always-on core (PRD/Spec/Story/Glossary). Additive and opt-in for ADR: a project that doesn't set docs.types keeps core behavior with no loss. Records that the registry capability is available; enables nothing. To adopt ADR, set docs.types to ["adr"] in storage.json (re-run setup-agent-kit's optional-doc-types question, or edit directly) and the kit creates the adrs/ subdir on first use.
steps.skipIfPresent: always idempotent — records availability only, enables nothing

steps.description: Glossary is now a core doc type — the single canonical home for every domain term. For filesystem doc providers, ensure the glossary/ subdir exists under docs.path. No-op for remote providers (the type is native) and for workspaces that already have a glossary dir.
steps.skipIfPresent: glossary subdir (or remote glossary type) already present under docs.path

steps.description: Migrate the distributed terms model to the glossary spine. For each domain term currently defined inline — in a Spec's Key concepts section or a PRD's inline product-term definitions — create a glossary note (glossary/<slug>.md) holding the canonical definition, then replace the inline definition with a [[term-slug]] citation. Spec Key concepts becomes an index of citations; the PRD cites. One owner per term: if the same term is defined in two places, reconcile to a single note and cite from both. This rewrites live doc-store content, so it is guided — per-term, human-in-the-loop, surfacing each proposed note and the citations that will replace the inline text before writing. Skip generic programming terms (they were never glossary material).
steps.skipIfPresent: no Spec Key concepts or PRD inline term definitions remain (all terms already live as glossary notes)

releases.summary: Story becomes a first-class requirement artifact; doc status ladder gains Proposed/Accepted/Implemented.

steps.description: Extend docs.statuses to the shared ladder draft|proposed|accepted|implemented|superseded|archived. Adds the role names if absent; preserves any project-custom display names already mapped.
steps.skipIfPresent: docs.statuses has accepted and implemented roles

steps.description: Add requirements.storyHome (default "docs") to storage.json. Selects the canonical home that owns story ID and status.

Remap existing docs at the old 'active' status to 'accepted' (the conservative floor — never falsely claim Implemented). Set 'implemented' only where a verifying-test trace confirms the behavior shipped. Touches every PRD/Spec/Story in the doc store.
steps.skipIfPresent: no docs remain at a legacy 'active' status

steps.description: For PRDs with inline user stories: extract each story to a Story artifact in the configured storyHome, and replace the PRD's inline bodies with a generated story index (link per story). Existing requirement IDs (e.g. MEM-US-1.2) remain valid citations — the story's home keeps them as its stable ID; only new stories use the home's native ID. Scenarios, edge cases, and acceptance criteria move to the Story.
steps.skipIfPresent: no PRD in the doc store contains inline story bodies
